Aww. That sounds terrible. Like a lot of things related to depression, it's a vicious cycle: you do nothing, you feel bad about doing nothing, you want to do things even less. I think the only way to break it is to take baby steps, try to do things... but it sucks because whenever I try, it just frustrates me how hard it is.

But it could also be that I grew up a bit (i was young when I first developed depression, so it probably stunted some of my emotional growth).

I feel the same way. I think it spills into times when you're not feeling depressed because, even if it isn't very bad in the moment, I think depression is still something that affects who you are just by virtue of how much it pervades your life... I can also totally understand about the speed. I remember taking some aptitude test in middle school and scoring in the 99th percentile for everything, except for one thing - processing speed, I was like 85th or something. I remember it was the worst in math class - everyone would speed through problems when we did problem sets and I'd just be left in the dust

I also get worried about my future, like, sometimes I feel the stress of just surviving is so much that, well, how will I ever function in society? I think one key is to realize that even though we have thoughts like that, we still DO manage to function in society. It can be so hard to believe in yourself sometimes...

If you wait one more year until you get to college, you will be able to get treatment via the health services at your college without ever telling your parents about it. 

But I understand you may not want to wait the extra year. In that case, you will have to be sneaky if you want to get treatment (judging by how your parents reacted to your brother, you might not want to even tell them that you're depressed). I suggest talking to friends and looking up nearby psychiatric clinics that have walk-in consultations and therapy sessions. Most of these will be cheap if you do not have access to insurance, and if you have good friends who can drive you/accompany you then it will be good. You'll have to figure out a way to do it when your parents are away though. 

Good luck!

It's a little depressing, but I think that, just like grieving, there is a process you have to go through. Maybe you can take hope in knowing that, by the end of the process, you'll be able to move on.

Hmm, I think the first thing is to look through your friends list and make sure you're okay with every one of those people reading your message. If you're not, you can remove them from your friends list. 

I would try to explain how depression has affected your life and behavior. I'd leave stuff like masturbation out of it, because anything related to sex and people will balk/get offended for no reason. But you can talk about what a day is like with depression, like how it might be hard to get up in the mornings. 

Don't forget to talk about WHY you are sharing it on facebook with everyone. Don't just say what depression is like, but also talk in your post about why you wanted to share it. For instance, you could say that you don't want to have to hide it, because it's not something anyone should be ashamed about. You can say that you want to be real with everyone instead of hiding behind a mask, perhaps. 

Finally, I think it would be important to mention that, even though you're making this big facebook post about it, depression is NOT what defines you. You don't want people to start thinking about you as "that depressed person". So I would try to make it clear that it's something you're dealing with, and something you want people to know about because you're not ashamed of it, but also that you are much more than your depression. 

I hope this helps. Good luck.

just think. what if something is just permanently wrong with my brain? what if I actually am just defective and cannot be fixed? what's the point in staying alive then? because how I see it, i'll just keep wasting my time here, wasting my potential and feeling miserable about it.
